A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TopoLM and retain the same core method and experiments. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching renumbered supplementary figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original TopoLM training and evaluation, spatial-selectivity analyses, and reanalysis of neural recordings. Table 1 reports original BLiMP, GLUE, and Brain-Score results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Topoformer-BERT evaluations, a spatial-permutation ablation, RSA brain-alignment results, and additional clustering analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, randomly permuted spatial grids, neighborhood-based spatial loss, and combined training objective remain unchanged. The model without spatial permutations is an added ablation, while the expanded explanation of permutations and neighborhood sampling documents the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain FineWeb-Edu training, language-localization and noun/verb/concreteness stimuli, BLiMP, GLUE, and the four neural datasets. The added analyses reuse this coverage. BookCorpus describes the imported Topoformer-BERT baseline's pretraining rather than a new dataset used to train TopoLM.

E2.justification: v1 discusses Topoformer only as related work. v2 evaluates pretrained Topoformer-BERT on language localization and semantic clustering in Sections 4–5 and Figures 13–14, adding a directly relevant alternative topographic method. The matched non-topographic control remains, and Table 1's comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds RSA evaluation on three retained neural datasets, significance-restricted Islands Moran's I scoring, and a control trained without spatial permutations. Section 4 also revises the written clustering threshold from p > 0.05 to p(FDR) < 0.05; this establishes a reported criterion revision, not that the original experiments were rerun. Core training and benchmark settings otherwise remain stable.

E4.justification: New Figure 12 tests whether removing spatial permutations lets activation patterns propagate across layers. Figure 14 examines whether clustering persists within statistically selective islands, distinguishing general smoothness from meaningful selectivity. Figure 6 adds an alternative RSA alignment analysis. Existing sampling and determiner-removal analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already report t-tests, FDR correction, and bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals from 10 cross-validation folds. The added RSA analysis uses the same uncertainty-reporting practice. No additional training-seed information or changed replication scheme is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 remains unchanged: TopoLM scores 0.71/0.68/0.78 versus 0.76/0.65/0.80 for the control. Substantial new findings include Topoformer-BERT's Hauptman clustering scores of 0.66 before sampling and 0.85 after sampling, despite few significant units, and the permutation-ablation results. New RSA results favor TopoLM on Pereira2018 but favor the control on Blank2014 and Fedorenko2016; these use a different metric from the retained linear-predictivity results.

T1.justification: Figure 14 introduces a limited new metric definition: compute Moran's I within islands of significant units and average across islands without weighting by island size. The training equations and Appendix A's standard Moran's I definition remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains that spatial smoothness produces brain-like language organization without fitting TopoLM to neural data, while largely preserving task performance and functional alignment. The abstract, introduction, and concluding synthesis retain this scope; the additional comparisons supply supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of why spatial permutations matter, why Topoformer-BERT may behave differently on sentences and isolated words, and why noisy normalization limits interpretation of RSA scores. It explicitly qualifies Topoformer-BERT as an unmatched baseline. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit limitation that the available neuroimaging datasets inadequately capture language topography and require further validation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer and access information for the Hauptman neural data, plus Topoformer-BERT's corpus, layer/head configuration, and activation-extraction locations. Existing TopoLM hyperparameters, hardware, and training time are retained. These are documentation and access additions; resource availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds BERT and BookCorpus references and expands the relationship to Topoformer, presenting local connectivity and spatial smoothness as related approaches to wiring-length minimization. The overall positioning as an extension of TDANN principles from vision to language remains intact.

P1.justification: The section and appendix organization is largely retained. v2 tightens prose, adds explanatory footnotes, renames Section 5 from syntactic and semantic clusters to semantic clusters, edits cross-references, consolidates duplicate references, and adds conference headers. These are localized revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with the RSA chart and new multipanel Figures 12–14 for the ablation, Topoformer-BERT maps, and clustering metrics. Existing supplementary Figures 6–10 largely become Figures 7–11. The cortical-surface display gains a t-value color scale, and Figure 2's displayed-block caption is revised.

improvement.justification: The added permutation ablation, alternative topographic baseline, clustering analyses, and code/data pointers improve scrutiny and reproducibility of the unchanged core method. The gain is limited by the unmatched comparator, Figure 6's contradictory claim of significance alongside p > 0.05, and removal of the explicit caveat about sparse neuroimaging coverage.
